title: Embedding service flow-control redesign: token-aware throttling & progressive scale-up
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Embedding endpoints are experiencing cascading latency spikes during multi-tenant bursts. Existing autoscaler reacts to queue depth too late, causing headroom churn and token-level p99 regressions for customers. We need a flow-control redesign that reduces tail latency, smooths scaling transitions, and enforces fair per-tenant token budgets without sacrificing throughput or unit-cost targets.

Scope: Implement a token-aware rate limiter + progressive scale-up policy for embedding routers, introduce request coalescing for duplicate embedding keys, expose backpressure signals in SDKs, and add observable SLOs for token wait-time and scale events. Work spans router, autoscaler, edge rate-limiter, and SDK surface.

Goals and targets: Reduce p99 request latency for embeddings by 30% under burst scenarios, reduce frequency of scale churn events by 50%, keep average per-token cost within 5% of baseline, and avoid increased 95th percentile cost for low-traffic tenants.

Out-of-scope: model-level quantization changes, embedding model architecture changes, and long-term forecasting engine (separate project).
proposed_solution: 1) Replace current request-count limiter with a token-aware leaky-bucket per-tenant and per-route limiter that considers sequence length distribution and embedding dims. 2) Progressive scale-up policy: on surge, provision 'warm-slices' within seconds instead of launching full pools; scale to target capacity in steps guided by moving-average token backlog. 3) Request coalescing: deduplicate identical embedding inputs for a short window at router to avoid redundant model invocations. 4) SDK backpressure hooks and retry guidance: SDKs receive 429 with 'retry-after' and optional reduced-dim fallback preference. 5) Add fairness arbitration: proportional-share when headroom is constrained so hot tenants cannot starve others. 6) Metrics and dashboards for token_wait_time, coalesced_hits, scale_step_events, and per-tenant headroom.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests simulate 1000-tenant burst and show <=30% p99 latency improvement vs baseline
Progressive scale-ups occur in <=30s for target+20% traffic bursts and avoid full cold pool launches
Token-based rate limiter prevents tenant overconsumption and preserves >=90% throughput for medium tenants
Coalescing reduces duplicate model invocations by >=20% in replayed production traces
SDKs surface retry-after and graceful fallback guidance in latest client release
risks: Coalescing introduces added latency for rare inputs due to dedupe window—must tune window to balance savings vs latency
Progressive warm-slice scheme may increase short-term costs if warm slices are underutilized
Per-tenant leaky-bucket requires storage of small token state at router; operational complexity when router restarts
Fairness arbitration may reduce absolute throughput for large paying tenants—need contracts check and opt-out path for reserved capacity
comments: 2026-02-26: Initial spike analysis complete. Replayed production traces: 72% of bursts are short (<=120s) and dominated by 10% of tenants.
2026-03-01: Design review with PM and SRE. Agreed to prototype token-aware limiter and progressive warm-slices first. Action: ENG-87654-arch-doc in Confluence.
2026-03-03: Implemented leaky-bucket PoC in router (branch: feat/token-limiter). Local load tests show 18% p99 improvement but higher tail for very long sequences.
2026-03-06: UX/SDK sync — agreed to include explicit 'retry_after_ms' and 'reduced_dim_suggestion' fields on 429 responses. PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/412
2026-03-08: Load replay using production traces (1h) with coalescing enabled reduced model calls by 26%. Noted edge-case: near-duplicate paraphrases not coalesced (future ML fuzzy-dedupe).
2026-03-10: Alpha deployment to canary region (us-east-1-canary). Observed expected warm-slice ramp behaviour; telemetry added to grafana panel 'embeddings.flow-control'
